sections.heading: Core Gameplay Mechanics
sections.body:
The core gameplay mechanics of Paper Scissor and Stone are simple yet engaging. The game is played between two players, with each player making one of three possible moves: Rock, Paper, or Scissors. The game's outcome is determined by the following rules: Rock beats Scissors, Scissors beats Paper, and Paper beats Rock. This may seem simple, but the game's strategy comes into play when you need to decide which move to make based on your opponent's previous moves.

The game also has a timer, which adds an element of pressure and excitement to the game. You need to make your move quickly, before the timer runs out. This makes the game more challenging and engaging, especially against tough opponents. The game's mechanics are also balanced, making it easy to win against weaker opponents and challenging to win against stronger opponents. This balance makes the game more engaging and replayable.

One of the things that I like about the game is its ability to be played in short sessions. You can play a quick game during your lunch break or between meetings.
